inputs.spec_clause_ref: kerml clause 8.2.3.4.1 (Namespaces.md, region_sha256 893fa9cef98e60fc) | sysml clause 8.2.2.5.1 (Packages.md, region_sha256 3ee603b1b89d4345)

decision: An optional visibility indicator, and nothing else, exactly as KerML 8.2.3.4.1 states it. Every membership production in the language opens with this, which is why it is a production of its own rather than an option repeated at each site.
notes:
THIS PRODUCTION IS NULLABLE, and that is the fact most likely to be needed elsewhere. It derives the empty string, so a site that writes `MemberPrefix?` accepts exactly what a site writing `MemberPrefix` accepts. That is the whole of the apparent KerML/SysML disagreement on ResultExpressionMember, and it is why that one is recorded rather than adjudicated.

The clause and the Xtext agree. The Xtext marks it `fragment`, which is a parser-generator inlining directive rather than a statement about the language, and is not carried across: this grammar keeps the production named because the specification names it.

FOR A PARSER AUTHOR: being nullable, this cannot be used to decide whether a member is starting. It consumes a `public`, `private` or `protected` if one is there and otherwise nothing, and the decision about what follows belongs to the enclosing production.

The empty corpus_instances is expected: the production contributes no terminal of its own beyond the VisibilityIndicator it optionally admits, and that terminal is attributable to VisibilityIndicator.

evidence.note: MemberPrefix is stated there as `( visibility = VisibilityIndicator )?`
the pilot fragment has the same body; only the `fragment` inlining directive differs
